LESSON: LINES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: GEOMETRY Strand Sub- strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experi
Topic 3.1: Lines
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Lines, part of GEOMETRY Strand Sub- strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experi in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do you make a line? 2. How are lines important in our life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify straight lines in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. draw straight lines on different surfaces,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify curved lines in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. draw curved lines on different surfaces,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. recognise straight and curved lines from real objects in the environment. ● Learners with blindness are given one on one activities that will enhance awareness of position of self in relation to how it is oriented in space. ● Learners stand behind one another facing the same side and identify what they have formed as a straight line by giving learners with blindness embossed/tactile cues on where to stand and a step-by- step guide on walking along the formed line. ● Learners are guided to mark two points on the ground and using a stick to join the two points to make a straight-line learner with blindness are given one on one hands on guidance on phenomena that require the use of sight. ● Learners with low vision practice 1. How do you make a line? 2. How are lines important in our life? 35 drawing straight lines on the ground and in their books while learners with blindness use glue and strings to fix thread on a surface forming a straight line. ● Learners with low vision form a semi- circle and one of them to draw a line around it and identify the semi- circle drawn as a curved line while learners with blindness move along the formed semi-circle while being given verbal cues on the curved line formed. ● In groups, learners with low vision practice drawing or making curved lines on the ground and on different surfaces ● Learners look for and identify lines from different objects in the environment. Core-Competencies to be developed: ● Learning to learn: The learner develops spatial reasoning and coordination skills, coupled with a learning-to-learn mind set, as learners mark two points on the ground and use a stick to join the two points to make a straight line.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Lines together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: The learner stands behind one another facing the same side and identify what they have formed as a straight line.

● Love: The learner works in groups and shares resources to draw lines on the ground.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self- awareness: The learner uses their hands to draw straight and curved lines.

Link to other learning areas:

● Movement and Creative Activities: The learner practises drawing or making curved lines on the ground and on

different surfaces.

Open place, strings, glue, sticks, tape measure, ruler, found objects
